root_review_proposal.exact_current_open_problem: For a knot $K$ in a compact oriented 3-manifold $Y$ whose exterior is irreducible, meaning every embedded sphere in its interior bounds a ball in the exterior, is each of the following equivalences true: (i) the enhanced A-polynomial has Newton polygon contained in an affine line if and only if the exterior admits a Seifert fibration over a disk with at most two exceptional circle fibres; and (ii) $K$ admits infinitely many distinct rational $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian surgeries if and only if the exterior admits a Seifert fibration over a disk with at most two exceptional circle fibres? An exceptional circle fibre has multiplicity greater than one.
root_review_proposal.proposed_open_problem:
Let $Y$ be a compact connected oriented smooth $3$-manifold and let $K\subset\operatorname{Int}Y$ be an oriented knot with irreducible exterior $E=Y\setminus\operatorname{Int}\nu K$. Choose a parametrized tubular neighborhood and an oriented integral basis $(\mu,\lambda)$ on its boundary torus $T$, where $\mu$ bounds a meridian disk in $\nu K$; $\lambda$ is a chosen framing, not an asserted preferred longitude. Any other components of $\partial E$ remain unfilled. For each primitive pair $(p,q)$, let $E(p\mu+q\lambda)$ mean filling only $T$ along that unoriented slope.

Form the Zariski closure $Z^{\mathrm{irr}}_{E,T}\subset(\mathbb C^*)^2$ of the peripheral eigenvalue pairs of irreducible $SL_2(\mathbb C)$ representations of $\pi_1(E)$, using the chosen basis. What additional hypotheses on this marked pair ensure that $Z^{\mathrm{irr}}_{E,T}$ has dimension at most one, so that its union of one-dimensional components can be represented by a primitive square-free Laurent equation (with the empty union represented by $1$)? Under those hypotheses, when are the following analogues valid: (i) the Newton polygon of that equation is contained in an affine line if and only if $E$ is Seifert fibered over a disk with at most two exceptional circle fibers; and (ii) infinitely many distinct primitive filling slopes on $T$ give $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian manifolds if and only if $E$ has that Seifert fibration? If additional boundary components or a two-dimensional peripheral image obstruct these analogues, what replacement geometric classification or formulation using the full peripheral vanishing ideal gives the correct statement? An exceptional circle fiber has multiplicity greater than one. No universal equivalence or universal one-dimensional peripheral-image assertion is assumed.
root_review_proposal.proposed_status: Open generalization problem. Baldwin–Sivek ask in Question 1.8 of arXiv:2405.19197v2 (28 November 2025; published in Math. Ann. 394 (2026)) whether their sphere-knot theorems have analogues for knots in other $3$-manifolds. The marked compact-manifold formulation above asks for the necessary hypotheses and replacement classification; it does not assert that the unqualified disk-base equivalences hold for manifolds with other boundary components. Indeed the core of a solid torus has exterior $T^2\times I$, no irreducible $SL_2(\mathbb C)$ representations, and abelian filling groups at every slope, but its two boundary tori preclude a Seifert fibration over a disk. The author’s search on 2026-10-19 found the source question and partial results, with no universal resolution identified. That bounded search observation is not evidence that no later resolution exists.
